query: How do review themes differ between positive and negative IMDb sentiment?

per_column.name: overall_verdict_tone
per_column.rationale: A graded sentiment verdict is essentially a re-encoding of label_pos itself; grouping on it against sentiment is near-tautological and yields little new relationship.

per_column.name: recommendation_stance
per_column.rationale: Recommend vs discourage is a direct proxy for positive/negative sentiment, so it largely restates the focus rather than opening an external association.

per_column.name: emotional_impact_on_reviewer
per_column.rationale: Positive/negative emotional valence tracks the sentiment label almost by definition; comparing it to label_pos reveals little beyond the label.

per_column.name: acting_quality_assessment
per_column.rationale: Praised/criticised/mixed for acting is a distinct thematic dimension with clean, interpretable categories that can be cross-tabulated against sentiment to reveal which aspects drive positivity.

per_column.name: directing_technical_quality
per_column.rationale: An independent evaluation of directing/technical craft; well-separated categories allow meaningful segmentation versus the sentiment focus.

per_column.name: primary_praise_target
per_column.rationale: Identifies WHAT is praised (plot, actor, writing, etc.), a genuinely thematic variable directly serving the 'review themes' query and enabling rich segmentation.

per_column.name: primary_criticism_target
per_column.rationale: Captures the theme of criticism; interpretable, well-separated categories ideal for comparing across positive vs negative reviews.

per_column.name: comparison_reference_valence
per_column.rationale: Whether the review compares favourably/unfavourably to other works is an external stylistic-thematic dimension, interpretable and groupable against sentiment.

judge.rationale: Five columns (acting, directing, praise target, criticism target, comparison valence) are strong thematic, interpretable segmentations that directly serve the 'which review themes differ by sentiment' query and are external to the focus. Three columns (overall_verdict_tone, recommendation_stance, emotional_impact_on_reviewer) are essentially graded restatements of the sentiment label and add little relational insight; several thematic columns also carry heavy not_present/NULL mass which slightly dilutes comparison power. As a set they support genuine exploratory analysis reasonably well, but the redundant sentiment re-encodings keep it short of excellent.
